Here are the missed findings for the Immune Response Layer.

FINDING_ID: IM_F022
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.85
DESCRIPTION: In `process_round()`, the orchestration flattens `cumulative_classes` into `cum_findings_flat` by extracting all `ec.members` before feeding it to `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round_from_findings()`. The detector then computes the cumulative cognitive yield as `Y = len(cumulative_findings) * h_bar`. This calculates yield using the raw count of all historical findings (including duplicates), violating the formal mathematical schema `Y = |F^(<=r)| * H_bar` where `F` is the quotient set of unique equivalence classes. Consequently, if models spam identical duplicates, the marginal value `mu(r)` will falsely spike, completely defeating the duplicate-penalizing intent of the Diminishing Returns component.
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the equivalence classes directly (or extract exactly one representative finding per class) when constructing `cum_findings_flat` and `new_findings_flat` in `process_round()` so that the yield scales strictly with novel flaw discovery.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F023
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: In `apply_diagnosis()`, if `_apply_transform()` returns `None` (which correctly occurs when a bounded parameter like `tau_vocab_growth` is already at its minimum floor), the method silently returns `None` without calling `set_remediation_state()` or incrementing the chain index. If this occurs on the very first step of a remediation chain (`chain_idx == 0`), the remediation state is never initialized. Because `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` cannot track or escalate non-existent state, the remediation chain permanently stalls at step 0 and the immune system will endlessly fire the same un-remediable diagnosis every round.
PROPOSED_FIX: If `_apply_transform()` returns `None`, immediately increment `chain_idx` and attempt the next fix in the sequence during the same round, or explicitly record an exhaustion event for that specific step so the chain can escalate naturally.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F024
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65
DESCRIPTION: When a remediation step is classified as `DEFER` in `apply_diagnosis()` (e.g., `findings_decline` step 0), it is appended to `_deferred_remediations` and the method immediately returns `None`. Because `_record_adjustment()` is bypassed, the deferred fix is never logged in `_immune_adjustments`. This completely circumvents the immune damping guard (`round_idx - adj["round"] < immune_damping_rounds`), which relies on the adjustment log to prevent oscillation. As a result, the immune layer will spam the queue with an identical, duplicate DEFER request every single round that the underlying pathology persists.
PROPOSED_FIX: Ensure that `DEFER` actions append a pending record to `_immune_adjustments` so the standard damping logic suppresses duplicate queueing of identical fixes while the operator's decision is pending.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F025
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60
DESCRIPTION: `reject_deferred_remediation()` updates the status of a queued human-review fix to `"REJECTED"`, but it completely fails to communicate this rejection to the immune layer's state tracking. It does not increment `chain_idx` in `_remediation_state`. Because the chain state is not advanced, and because DEFER queueing bypasses damping (see IM_F024), rejecting a deferred remediation causes the immune layer to immediately re-diagnose the unresolved pathology and perpetually queue new identical DEFER requests for the exact same rejected step.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `reject_deferred_remediation()`, advance the `chain_idx` for the rejected pathology in `_remediation_state` so the immune layer knows to escalate to the next tier of the remediation chain in the subsequent round.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F026
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50
DESCRIPTION: `record_dispatch_success_after_block()` is completely orphaned within `DynamicManager`. While `record_dispatch_block()` is correctly wired into `check_dispatch_feasibility()`, there is no internal invocation within `process_round()` to register when a previously blocked model successfully returns a valid response. Because `dispatch_successes` remains permanently empty, Pathology 4 (Dispatch False Positive) in `check_dispatch_health()` is dead code and can never autonomously trigger unless an external orchestrator breaks encapsulation to manually populate the success array.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, iterate through `responses`. For any model that successfully returned a parseable response, verify if it exists in `_dispatch_blocks`. If so, invoke `record_dispatch_success_after_block()` internally before running the health monitor checks.
VERIFIED: TRUE
